record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: Should all measured features or attributes be weighted equally in an instance-based learning rule, and if not, how should the feature weights be selected?

evidence.quote: Should all the features (attributes) we weighted equally and if not how should the feature weights be chosen?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an instance-based (lazy) learning rule that classifies a query point x ∈ ℝ^n by comparing it to a stored set of labeled training instances {(x_i, y_i)}_{i=1}^N using a parameterized distance of the form

   d_w(x, x') = ( Σ_{j=1}^n w_j · ρ(x_j, x'_j) )^{1/2},

where w = (w_1, …, w_n) is a vector of nonnegative feature weights and ρ is a per-feature dissimilarity (e.g. squared difference for numeric features, 0/1 mismatch for symbolic features). The prediction at x is obtained from the labels of the nearest stored instances under d_w (e.g. by k-nearest-neighbor voting).

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether the uniform choice w_1 = w_2 = … = w_n (equal weighting of all measured features/attributes) is, in general, an appropriate choice for such a learning rule, in the sense of minimizing expected generalization error over arbitrary learning problems.

(b) If equal weighting is not appropriate, provide a principled, general method for selecting the weight vector w from the training data (and any available prior information about feature relevance), and justify the choice by characterizing the class of problems on which the method yields provably good predictive performance.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and reviews of feature weighting methods for lazy/instance-based learning algorithms (k-NN and its variants) continue to be published, and recent literature explicitly states that determining a generally optimal weighting scheme remains an unsolved challenge. Numerous filter, wrapper, supervised/unsupervised, and global/local weighting techniques have been developed, but no universal solution exists, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Feature weighting methods: A review
status_evidence.snippet: Extensive review of state-of-the-art feature weighting methods, classifying them by learning strategy, methodology, and feedback; notes open challenges remain.
status_evidence.claim: Feature weighting is still an active research area with unresolved challenges for choosing optimal weights.

status_evidence.title: A Review and Empirical Evaluation of Feature Weighting Methods for a Class of Lazy Learning Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Many k-NN variants have been proposed to reduce sensitivity by parameterizing the distance function with feature weights.
status_evidence.claim: No single feature weighting method is established as universally optimal for instance-based learners.
